answer: Each agent identity requires a hardware-bound credential plus a stake of 200 units locked for 40 epochs, with registry entries chained to a summit of cosigned checkpoints. A sybil attacker locking N stakes forfeits 100 percent on detection and waits 40 epochs per credential, and the jetty of pending withdrawals holds funds until jurors confirm. Splitting identities multiplies the locked stake and shared slashing risk, so marginal cost per fake identity stays at 200 units and independent jurors trace each credential to one sable record.
